classification.difficultyReason: Model the dilution by recognising that sampling preserves concentration while adding water multiplies it by 500/600, then apply that unsupplied factor over 20 cycles.

content.prompt: I take $500\text{ mL}$ of a liquid and dilute it with $100\text{ mL}$ of water. Then I take $500\text{ mL}$ of the mixture and again dilute it with $100\text{ mL}$ of water. I repeat this process $20$ times in all. What percentage of the final mixture, by volume, is original liquid? Give your answer correct to $1$ decimal place.

answer.short:
The final mixture contains approximately $2.6\%$ original liquid by volume.

Each dilution multiplies the concentration by $\frac56$. As a percentage of the initial $500\text{ mL}$, the original liquid retained is approximately $3.13\%$.
answer.worked:
Each dilution makes $600\text{ mL}$ from $500\text{ mL}$, so the concentration is multiplied by $\frac{500}{600}=\frac56$ each time. Let $C_{20}$ be the percentage concentration after $20$ dilutions.

$$\begin{align*}C_{20}&=100\left(\frac56\right)^{20}\%\\C_{20}&\approx2.6\%\end{align*}$$

This is the interpretation used by the supplied answer. If the question instead asks for the quantity retained as a percentage of the initial $500\text{ mL}$, the first dilution removes none of the original liquid, and the subsequent $19$ selections each retain $\frac56$ of it. Let $V_{20}$ be the original liquid remaining.

$$\begin{align*}V_{20}&=500\left(\frac56\right)^{19}\text{ mL}\\V_{20}&\approx15.65\text{ mL}\\\text{Percentage retained}&=\frac{500(5/6)^{19}}{500}\times100\%\\\text{Percentage retained}&\approx3.13\%\end{align*}$$
